title: Maryland's 6th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: This race will determine the U.S. Representative for Maryland's 6th Congressional District, a competitive district that stretches from the western Maryland panhandle through Frederick County and into the northern suburbs of Montgomery County. Incumbent Democrat April McClain Delaney, first elected in 2024, is seeking a second term and faces a notable primary challenge from former Congressman David Trone, whom she succeeded. The Republican primary features three candidates including Marine veteran Chris Burnett, perennial candidate Robin Ficker, and Air Force veteran Mariela Roca, who is making her third run for the seat. The general election is expected to be closely contested given the district's political diversity, with the primary scheduled for June 23, 2026, and the general election on November 3, 2026.
polling_note: No independent general-election polls were found for Maryland's 6th Congressional District as of June 13, 2026. The New York Times poll tracker lists the district but had not published specific general-election poll data. The primary is still ahead (June 23, 2026), so general-election polling is not yet available.

candidates.name: April McClain Delaney
candidates.summary: April McClain Delaney is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Maryland's 6th Congressional District, first elected in 2024. She previously served as Deputy Administrator of the National Telecommunications and Information Administration under President Biden and founded the Washington, D.C. office of Common Sense Media, a children's advocacy nonprofit. She is running for re-election on a platform focused on affordability, protecting social safety nets, and expanding rural broadband access.

candidates.name: David Trone
candidates.summary: David Trone served as the U.S. Representative for Maryland's 6th Congressional District from 2019 to 2025 before running unsuccessfully for the U.S. Senate in 2024. He is the co-founder and former president of Total Wine & More, the largest privately owned beer, wine, and spirits retailer in the United States. Trone is challenging his successor, April McClain Delaney, in the Democratic primary, emphasizing his experience in Congress and business background.

candidates.name: Alexis Goldstein
candidates.summary: Alexis Goldstein is a former financial regulatory expert at the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau who was fired in early 2026 after a confrontation with DOGE staff, which she cites as a catalyst for her congressional campaign. She previously worked on Wall Street as a programmer and analyst before joining the Occupy Wall Street protests and later became a financial policy director at the Open Markets Institute. Goldstein is running as a progressive Democrat focused on financial regulation, consumer protection, and economic inequality.

candidates.name: George Gluck
candidates.summary: George Gluck is a perennial candidate who has run for office multiple times, previously as a Green Party candidate and now seeking the Democratic nomination for Maryland's 6th Congressional District. He describes himself as a 'prudent progressive' and believes the political climate under the Trump administration may present a stronger opportunity for his candidacy. Gluck has been an active presence in local politics for over a decade.

candidates.name: Christopher Burnett
candidates.summary: Chris Burnett is a retired Marine Corps officer who served for 24 years, including deployments to Iraq and assignments at U.S. Southern Command and Marine Forces Cyberspace Command. He is a legal scholar and attorney running as an America First conservative focused on restoring trust in government. Burnett emphasizes his military leadership experience and promises to bring accountability to Congress.

candidates.name: Robin Ficker
candidates.summary: Robin Ficker is a perennial political candidate, former Maryland state delegate (1979-1983), and disbarred attorney who has run for numerous offices over five decades. He is a real estate broker and political activist known for his colorful campaign style and frequent ballot appearances. Ficker has run for Congress, Senate, governor, and county executive multiple times since the 1970s.

forecast.rationale: No general-election or primary polls are available, and the June 23 primary is still three days away, so uncertainty is unusually high. The Democratic primary is notably competitive — incumbent April McClain Delaney faces a serious challenge from former Rep. David Trone, a wealthy self-funder who held the seat for three terms. On the Republican side, the field lacks a standout candidate: Marine veteran Chris Burnett is a credible first-time candidate but faces perennial candidate Robin Ficker and two-time prior loser Mariela Roca. Structurally, MD-06 has a D+2 PVI and has been held by Democrats since 2019, with Delaney winning 54-46 in 2024. However, without polling data and with an unsettled nomination on both sides — particularly a divisive D-primary that could weaken or change the Democratic standard-bearer — only a very narrow Democratic edge is justified. This forecast should be revisited once the primary produces nominees and general-election polling becomes available.
